title: Book Three · Chapter 130: A Page for the Wait
story:
On the second Friday, a woman comes to ask about a sewing table.

Her small son follows her into the workshop. He looks at the front shelves, then opens a little drawer on display.

His mother turns at the sound.

“Leave that.”

He closes it. A moment later, his hand moves toward it again.

Ronan comes around the counter.

“Would you like to draw?”

The boy looks up.

Ronan finds a blank piece of paper and the short pencil. He puts both on a low stool beside the counter.

The boy sits down. His mother thanks Ronan, then opens her own paper.

The boy sits beside the stool and bends over his page. The pencil pushes one corner onto the floor.

Ronan picks the page up before anyone steps on it.

“Keep your other hand here.”

He rests one finger on the empty corner. The boy puts his own hand in its place.

“Like that?”

“Yes.”

The boy draws a long line. His hand moves with the pencil, and the paper begins to slide again.

Ronan moves the stool nearer the wall. The boy shifts around it and finds room for his elbow.

He tries the line once more. This time, it reaches the other side of the page.

Ronan steps back to the counter. The boy calls him again, but his mother has a question too.

“I will look in a moment,” Ronan tells him.

The boy adds something to his line. His mother spreads her drawing flat, and Ronan gives her room to show it.

Mr Sun is finishing with another customer. Ronan looks at the woman's drawing while they wait.

There is a sewing machine at one end of a table. She has written a size below it.

“Is that the space for the machine?” he asks.

“For the whole table.”

“Where will the cloth go?”

She points to the empty side. Ronan thinks of Mum's sleeve work across their table.

He asks about a longer piece of cloth. The woman opens her arms to show him.

“Like this.”

They look at the drawing again. She makes a note about the clear space beside the machine.

Mr Sun comes over. Ronan shows him the note and steps back while they discuss the table.

The little boy lifts his page.

It shows a round face with a great deal of hair. There are two small ears near the bottom.

“Who is that?” his mother asks.

He points to Mr Sun.

Mr Sun takes the page and looks at it. Then he touches the thin hair above his own forehead.

“Some for next year too.”

The woman laughs. Ronan gives the boy a second blank page, and the adults finish their talk.

When they leave, the boy takes both drawings. He shuts the little display drawer carefully on his way past.

At twelve, Mr Sun pays Ronan the second week's six yuan. He has now earned twelve in all. After the one yuan for peanuts, eleven remains in his work envelope.

Ronan puts today's date beside the first one.

Mr Sun looks at the empty stool.

“A busy little artist.”

“He gave you more hair.”

“You could use that pencil yourself.”

Ronan looks at the short end, then at his own dark hair. Mr Sun smiles and takes the pencil back to the counter. Ronan puts the stool in its place before he leaves for lunch.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

on display＝摆出来供人看的；sewing machine＝缝纫机；forehead＝额头；remain＝剩下。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样让等待的孩子有事可做？他又问清了缝纫桌的什么需要？
2. 第二周领钱后累计挣了多少？扣掉唯一的一元花生钱，工资信封余多少？

## 读句子

**He has now earned twelve in all.**

拆开看：He / has now earned / twelve / in all.

他／现在已经挣得／十二元／合计。
